observed_reality: The accepted self-hosted Ubuntu lane baseline /usr/bin/python3 loads SQLite 3.45.1, not a fixed SQLite runtime.
The exact baseline mapped libsqlite3 object is /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsqlite3.so.0.8.6 with SHA-256 f2cd05de8b6f71ea9d0495a6f9ff9cae844b15d9c45b7ef49ee0af0f81658cc7.
Official SQLite 3.53.4 is technically loadable by the same /usr/bin/python3 via a disposable rootless overlay, but that is not production binding.

Fresh main proved that V4 admits two byte-distinct self-consistent SQLite 3.53.4 builds when the caller supplies the corresponding manifest digest, so caller-selected consistency is not deployment authority.

Fresh main now contains an OS-owned V5 candidate that fixes the trust-anchor path at /etc/frank-v0.1/sqlite-runtime-anchor-v1.json, requires non-root Frank runtime, checks root-owned/non-writable ancestor chain, rejects symlinks, checks opened-inode continuity, pins manifest/library/version/source-id, and binds parent/child re-exec to the same anchor digest.

The fresh-main V5 target workflow completed as a measurement workflow but its mechanism receipt is BLOCKED_ROOT_ANCHOR_POSITIVE_NOT_RUN because sudo_nopasswd=false; positive root-owned-anchor execution and full fixed-SQLite process admission were not run.
This worker's overlapping V5 draft PR #418 was closed without merge after fresh main superseded it.
grf.leading_hypothesis: Release-safe WAL persistence requires exact active-library attestation plus an independently authorized OS/deployment trust anchor that the Frank process or caller cannot choose.
grf.strongest_counterhypothesis: Caller-selected manifest digest plus internal artifact consistency is sufficient to authorize the runtime.
grf.collapse: The strongest counterhypothesis is refuted. Main V5 is now the preferred implementation lineage, but the independent root-owned anchor positive path remains privilege-blocked on the current self-hosted Actions runner and production admission remains unproved.

upstream_evidence.sqlite_wal_reset_affected: 3.7.0 through 3.51.2 under documented concurrent writer/checkpoint conditions

negative_results: CLI/package version is not sufficient evidence for the SQLite library loaded by Python.
The measured accepted-lane baseline still loads SQLite 3.45.1.
V4 caller-supplied manifest consistency is not independent runtime authorization.
The current self-hosted Actions runner does not provide passwordless sudo, so the positive root-owned V5 anchor path cannot be established from that lane.

unusual_experiment.description: A temporary fake sqlite3 CLI reported 3.53.4 while Python in the same environment reported its actually loaded SQLite 3.46.1; the temporary decoy was deleted immediately after measurement.
unusual_experiment.note: Fresh-main V5 workflow contains code for an atomic-replace unusual experiment, but that branch did not execute because sudo_nopasswd=false; it is not counted as an executed experiment in this cycle.

release_adjudication.reason: Accepted-lane baseline is SQLite 3.45.1. Main V5 materially improves the independent OS trust-anchor design, but its positive root-owned anchor path and full fixed-SQLite process admission were not executed, the production anchor is not provisioned, and non-bypassable product boot/persistence routing is unproved.
